title: Demonstration Experiments
summary: Adaptive experiments are used extensively in online platforms, healthcare and biotechnology, and the social sciences. Often, the primary goal is not to precisely estimate a treatment effect but to demonstrate that at least one candidate intervention yields a positive effect, for some subpopulation and on some measured outcome. We formalize this objective as testing the global null in a threshold bandit framework, and develop two inference procedures that are valid under general adaptive sampling: one that pools information across promising arms, and one based on time-uniform multiple testing…
